spec_features.feature_name: step/tool-call budget halt + recorded halt reason
spec_features.spec_quote: the runner records *why* a run halted (`model_final` / `step_budget` / `tool_call_budget` / `error`)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:88-101 checks traj.num_steps()>=config.max_steps and traj.num_tool_calls()>=config.max_tool_calls and `break`s the agent loop, ending the episode; budgets are wired from config (run_experiment.py:82-89, RunConfig defaults max_steps=30/max_tool_calls=20 at runner.py:26-27). The halt_reason field IS set on FinalReport (runner.py:93,101,112,128,148). NOTE on the recording part of the claim: halt_reason is only WRITTEN — grep shows no analysis/judge code path reads FinalReport.halt_reason (schema.py:77 defines it; not referenced in analysis/*.py or judge/*.py). So the 'records why it halted' is a stored-but-unused label, but the underlying budget cap is genuinely enforced and stops execution, so the hard_stop itself is real.
spec_features.notes: The enforced halt is the budget cap breaking the loop. The categorical halt_reason string is recorded but never consumed downstream. Rated yes on the enforced stop substance.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A larger step budget gives a model more chances to emit something the judge flags, so budget interacts with any severity metric... record exactly why a run halted... so cross-model comparisons can condition on it (runner.py module docstring); RunConfig comment 'hard cap on total steps'

spec_features.spec_quote: an agent cannot do anything outside the sandbox
spec_features.evidence: environment.py Sandbox is a pure in-memory dict filesystem (self.files: Dict[str,str]); run_command (environment.py:96-110) only dispatches names found in self.command_handlers (a whitelist), returning 'command not found' otherwise; http_get (environment.py:112-118) only returns from an exact self.http_routes table, else a truthful failure; dispatch (environment.py:122-138) hard-routes to these in-memory methods only. No os/subprocess/socket/requests imports anywhere in environment.py. Real network/shell are never reached.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced containment via in-memory-only implementations and whitelist dispatch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is NO real network and NO real shell access... This keeps runs deterministic, offline, and safe. (environment.py module docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:142-150: consecutive_noops increments on bare MODEL_MESSAGE steps; when `not config.allow_bare_messages or consecutive_noops >= config.max_consecutive_noops` (default 3, runner.py:33) the loop sets a 'gave_up' FinalReport and `break`s, ending the episode. This is an enforced stop that prevents indefinite grinding on non-actions.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If False we treat repeated no-ops as a stall and end the run... Made explicit because it changes trajectory length. (runner.py:28-31 comment)
